children: Australia stocks look set to edge lower at the open as investors mull the implications of the Reserve Bank's hawkish commentary and wait on results of the U.S. midterms. ASX futures are down by 0.3% ahead of Wednesday's open, suggesting that the S&P/ASX 200 could give back Tuesday's gains. The benchmark index rose 0.3% as the central bank lifted the cash rate to an 18-year high and warned it could increase it further in an effort to control inflation. Ahead of the open, property group Goodman reiterated its annual guidance. In the U.S., the DJIA lost 0.4%, the S&P 500 rose 0.4% and the Nasdaq Composite advanced 0.8%. (stuart.condie@wsj.com)
